# v1.1.0-dev.110: The app window stays honest

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.109`.

## Deleting a virtual window asks properly

Deleting a virtual window used to need a second press of Delete within five
seconds. It asks with a proper confirmation modal now, from every surface
that can delete one, and declining leaves everything exactly as it was.

## Dialogs no longer leave the main window behind

An audit that traced every mutation to the interface update it should cause
found a family of bugs where a change made inside a dialog never reached
the main window:

- A profile duplicated from its dialog never appeared in the sidebar.
- Restoring a saved version from the History dialog left the window on the
  old copy, and the next edit quietly saved that old copy back over the
  restore.
- Saving or clearing display settings, saving a remap-as-new from the
  auto-activation chooser, and setting or clearing a hotkey had the same
  problem.
- Renaming or duplicating a profile silently dropped its virtual-window
  assignments out of the window's view until an unrelated refresh.
- Hiding a container to the tray left its title bar tab floating on screen.
- Renaming a shared container from the page didn't reach a container that
  was open. Releasing a splitter on one didn't reach the page's diagram.
- Auto-activation's best-guess left the details pane's saved time stale.

All fixed. The sidebar's own add/delete/re-add logic was verified honest
through the real flows and is pinned by a new probe.

## A Load says what it started

When a Load starts windows (an app-wide "always start new" default, say),
the status line names them and the toast counts them, instead of folding
them into "restored". If terminals have been opening on every Load, look
for "started N new" here: the cause is a start default set in a window
editor row, under "When a profile loads".

## Smaller fixes

- The two remaining guard-incompatible probes were re-run bare: a docked
  window never stays maximized (14 checks green), and the caption-colour
  probe's pixel legs were environment-blocked, not failing.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
